title: Middle projection and composable-pair map for a restricted scheme relation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R,U,U'$ be schemes over $S$, and let $s,t:R\to U$ and $q:U'\to U$ be morphisms over $S$. Write $R'=U'\times_{q,U,s}R\times_{t,U,q}U'$ with endpoint maps $s',t':R'\to U'$ as in [def-sfb-restricted-groupoid-relation], using the scheme fibre products of [def-pc-fibre-product]. The middle projection $m:R'\to R$ sends $(x,r,y)$ to $r$ on every test-scheme point. Concretely, for $R'=(U'\times_{q,U,s}R)\times_{t\circ\operatorname{pr}_R,U,q}U'$, it is the composite of the projection to the first factor $U'\times_U R$ and the projection from that factor to $R$. The canonical map on composable pairs $\kappa:R'\times_{s',U',t'}R'\to R\times_{s,U,t}R$ is induced by $m$ on both factors: $\operatorname{pr}_1\circ\kappa=m\circ\operatorname{pr}_1$ and $\operatorname{pr}_2\circ\kappa=m\circ\operatorname{pr}_2$. Thus it sends a composable pair of triples to the pair of their middle coordinates. These maps are defined for arbitrary $s,t,q$; no groupoid, monicity, etaleness or covering hypothesis is imposed.
